2.  24-52918  Recommendation to receive and file a report from the Director of Health and

  Alison King, Director of Health and Human Services, provided the following
  information to the Board:

  • A recap of the 2024 Public Health Week Conference the Department held on
  April 4, 2024.
  • Notification of the activation of the Department Operations Center in
  response to a local TB outbreak, and the potential for the City to declare a
  local public health emergency.
  • The Department is also currently monitoring for measles.
  • Ms. King’s recent trip to Washington, DC for the National Association of
  Housing and Redevelopment Officials Annual Conference, and her meetings
  with elected officials.
  • The upcoming presentation of the Health Department’s 2025 budget.

  Board member Betancourt joined the meeting at 8:02 a.m.

  The Board briefly discussed drafting a letter of support and/or op-ed article
  addressing the current TB outbreak, the importance of local public health and the
  need for increased funding to be responsive to such events.

  A motion was made by Member Walton, seconded by Member Lesen, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

5.  24-52990  Recommendation to discuss Board Goals and Infrastructure.

  James Suazo, Executive Director of Long Beach Forward, continued his facilitation
  of the Board’s strategic planning process. Mr. Suazo recapped the process to date
  and shared with the Board activities identified from the previous sessions. The
  Board then took the time to review these activities and then met in small group
  discussions to prioritize each activity in order of importance to the Board’s future
  goals.

  A motion was made by Member St Bernard, seconded by Member Vaias, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  11 Schwerin, St Bernard, Betancourt, Gupta, Lesen, McNeeley, Red
  Eagle, Tejani, Vaias, Walton, Van Meeveren
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 4 Sanders, Curtis, Girgis, Clark

6.  24-52991  Recommendation to discuss a proposal for the City to install beach water hazard
  signage along City waterways.

  Board member St. Bernard discussed the need to ensure that the public is informed
  of beach water quality issues, and any closures of local beaches due to poor water
  quality or health hazards. In addition to the current methods of informing the public,
  through social media and the City’s website, the Board discussed drafting a
  recommendation to the Mayor and Council to install permanent signage along City
  recreational water areas that would indicate whether a beach was safe for human
  or animal contact.

  A motion was made by , seconded by , to approve recommendation and to
  submit a letter of recommendation to the Mayor and City Council advocating
  for the installation of permanent signage along City beaches and recreational
  water areas advising the public of the current water quality and safety for
  human and animal contact. . The motion by the following vote:
